details:
**Succeeded Liz Truss as prime minister**
Sunak became the Conservative British prime minister in October 2022, after Liz Truss resigned following only about 49 days in office. He was the first British prime minister of Indian descent and the first Hindu to hold the office, and he served until July 2024.

**First prime minister appointed by King Charles III**
Sunak was the first prime minister invited to form a government by King Charles III, who became king in September 2022. Truss had been appointed by Queen Elizabeth II two days before the queen's death.

**Chancellor of the Exchequer resignation**
Sunak served as Chancellor of the Exchequer (Britain's finance minister) under Boris Johnson from 2020 to 2022. He resigned in July 2022, the same evening as Health Secretary Sajid Javid, after the Chris Pincher scandal: Johnson had promoted Pincher despite knowing of misconduct allegations against him. A wave of resignations followed that forced Johnson out.

**2022 leadership contest and "fairytale economics"**
In the summer 2022 Conservative leadership election to replace Johnson, Sunak finished second to Liz Truss in the vote of party members. During the campaign he attacked her plans for unfunded tax cuts as "fairytale" economics that could cause an "inflationary spiral." After her mini-budget crashed the markets, his warnings seemed justified.

**Partygate fine**
In April 2022, police fined Sunak, along with Boris Johnson, for breaking COVID lockdown rules by attending a gathering held for Johnson's birthday in June 2020 at 10 Downing Street. Johnson is a former mayor of London.

**Infosys and Akshata Murty**
Sunak's wife, Akshata Murty, is the daughter of N. R. Narayana Murthy, a co-founder of the Indian IT giant Infosys. Her shares in the company make the family very wealthy, and her non-domiciled tax status caused controversy in 2022.

**Winter Economy Plan**
A package of measures Sunak announced as chancellor in September 2020 to support jobs and businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic. It replaced the furlough scheme with a new job-support scheme. Sunak was also known for the furlough program and the "Eat Out to Help Out" restaurant discount scheme.

**Forests and Climate Leaders' Partnership (FCLP)**
An international initiative that Sunak helped launch at the COP27 climate summit in Egypt in November 2022 to halt and reverse forest loss by 2030. At the launch he said that "for too long the world's forests have been undervalued and underestimated."

**"100% of women don't have penises"**
Comments Sunak made in a 2023 interview defending his view of biological sex in the debate over transgender rights. He added that people should show "tolerance for those who are thinking about changing their gender."

**2024 general election defeat**
Sunak called an early general election for July 2024, announcing it in the rain outside Downing Street. The Conservatives lost in a landslide to Keir Starmer's Labour Party, and Sunak stepped down as party leader. Kemi Badenoch succeeded him.

**Rwanda plan and "Stop the boats"**
Sunak's signature immigration policy aimed to deter migrants crossing the English Channel in small boats by deporting asylum seekers to Rwanda. "Stop the boats" was one of his five main pledges, but legal challenges kept the deportation flights from taking off.

**Windsor Framework**
A 2023 agreement Sunak negotiated with the European Union that revised the post-Brexit Northern Ireland Protocol and eased trade checks between Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
